claims.text: Increasing Al concentration in AlxCrCoFeNi high-entropy nanoalloys enhances high-temperature structural stability.
Increasing Al concentration in AlxCrCoFeNi high-entropy nanoalloys enhances high-temperature chemical stability.
Increasing Al modifies the local electronic structure and atomic-size mismatch.
The Al-induced electronic and size-mismatch changes trigger a transition from chemical clustering to ordering.
Low-Al (x = 0.1) and high-Al (x = 1.0) nanoalloys initially have predominantly disordered, chemically clustered configurations under ambient conditions.
Local electronic structure and atomic-size mismatch mediate the balance between chemical clustering and ordering.
Higher Al content changes the electron-density distribution.
Higher Al content reduces lattice strain arising from atomic-size differences.
The electronic and strain changes caused by higher Al lower the activation barrier for high-temperature ordering.
The low-Al alloy lacks the electronic and size-mismatch driving force for ordering and consequently remains clustered.
Differences in ordering behavior underpin differences in high-temperature stability.
Between approximately 600 °C and 900 °C, the high-Al alloy will undergo an ordering transition.
The proposed ordering transition will produce XRD peak splitting and altered XRD and PDF features.
TEM or atom-probe tomography will independently confirm the high-Al alloy's ordering transition.
The low-Al alloy will retain a more disordered, clustered structure than the high-Al alloy under identical heating conditions.
The prediction is limited to 600–900 °C under an inert atmosphere.
